Pattern Observed: Client said 'just a few data sources' — turned out to be 15 with undocumented dependencies
What Went Wrong (or Right): Scoped for 5 sources, actually needed 15. Timeline blew out by 6 weeks.
Root Cause: Trusted the client's estimate without verifying. Didn't ask to see the source systems before committing.
What I'd Do Differently: Always do a source system inventory in discovery — count them myself, don't take the client's word for it.

Pattern Observed: The real decision-maker wasn't in the room
What Went Wrong (or Right): Designed the architecture, got sign-off, then the CTO (who wasn't involved) rejected it.
Root Cause: Didn't map the actual decision-making chain. Assumed the people in meetings had authority.
What I'd Do Differently: Ask early: 'Who else needs to approve this?' and 'Has this kind of decision been overturned before?'

Pattern Observed: Built a generic ingestion framework for 3 sources
What Went Wrong (or Right): Spent 2 weeks on a reusable framework when copy-paste-modify would have taken 3 days.
Root Cause: Wanted to build it 'properly.' The client didn't need generic — they needed done.
What I'd Do Differently: Use the complexity check. 3 sources don't justify a framework. 15 might.
